settings.question: Are Corvo rugs made to order?
settings.answer: Yes. Every Corvo rug is made to order in our Portuguese atelier, hand-tufted for the room it will live in.

settings.question: Can I customize the size, shape and colours?
settings.answer: Yes. Dimensions, shape, materials and an infinite range of colours can all be tailored to your project. We prepare samples for your approval before production begins.

settings.question: How do I start a bespoke project?
settings.answer: On the Tailor your rug page: see a price guide for your idea and ask for a proposal. You can also write to us through the contact page. From there, the path is simple: consultation, design, sampling, production.

settings.question: What materials do you use?
settings.answer: [materials_count] materials. [materials_standard] are included in the price of every rug. [materials_plus] add a supplement. [materials_premium] are rare fibres with a price of their own. The Raw materials page describes each one and what it adds to the price.

settings.question: What does delivery cost, and do you deliver abroad?
settings.answer: We deliver worldwide. Delivery is not included in the price of a rug: it is quoted for each order, by destination and size, and confirmed with you after you order.

settings.question: How long does a rug take?
settings.answer: A rug is made to order and ships in [lead_weeks] weeks. With priority production it ships in [priority_weeks] weeks, for [priority_percent]% more. A custom colour, design or shape can take longer, and we confirm the date with your order.

settings.question: Do you work with interior designers and architects?
settings.answer: Yes. We offer dedicated trade support and sampling. Write to us to join the programme.

settings.question: How is the price of a rug worked out?
settings.answer: By area. Each design has a craft level, which sets its price per m², from [from_price] per m². Every rug page shows the price of its five standard sizes and works out the price of any other size, up to [max_size], as you type it. Prices include VAT.

settings.question: Can I see a sample first?
settings.answer: Yes. A [sample_size] sample of any rug costs [sample_price]. Order it from the page of the rug or from the Samples page.

settings.question: Can I change or cancel an order?
settings.answer: Yes, up to [change_hours] business hours after we confirm your order.

settings.question: What if something is wrong with my rug?
settings.answer: Every rug passes a quality control and is photographed before it leaves us. If you find a defect, tell us in writing within [claim_days] business days of receiving the rug, with photographs.

settings.question: Will the colours match exactly?
settings.answer: Colour can vary slightly between dye batches. This is normal in any textile and is not a defect.

settings.question: Can I return a rug?
settings.answer: No. Every rug is made to order for its buyer, so it cannot be returned or exchanged. An order can still be changed or cancelled up to [change_hours] business hours after we confirm it.

settings.question: Which colours can I choose?
settings.answer: Any colour. Every colour of a design can be changed: to one of the [palette_count] colours of the Open Palette at no extra cost, or to any other colour, matched to your reference, for [colour_price] per colour. The Colours page shows how.

settings.question: What is the largest rug you can make?
settings.answer: [max_size]. Every design can be made to measure in any size up to that, and its rug page works out the price as you type the size.

settings.question: How much does a bespoke rug cost?
settings.answer: From [from_price] per m², VAT included. The price per m² follows the craft level of the design, on a scale of 1 to [level_count]. The material, the pile, the size and custom colours can add to it. The Tailor your rug page works out a price guide for your idea.

settings.content: Write to our design concierge — replies within one business day.

settings.title: Care & FAQ
settings.text: How to care for a rug, how to choose its size, and plain answers on prices, delivery and orders.
settings.image_alt: A plain cream rug in a sunlit room with a wooden chair and a console table

settings.title: Keeping a rug at its best
settings.text: A few habits keep a rug in excellent condition over time.
settings.image_alt: The pile of a cream rug seen from close, in sunlight

settings.label: Vacuuming
settings.value: Once or twice a week, with a vacuum cleaner without rotating brushes, which would damage the fibres. A high pile may need it more often.

settings.label: A new rug
settings.value: A rug in natural materials may pill during its first months. This is normal and lessens with time.

settings.label: Spills
settings.value: Act quickly. Absorb liquids with a highly absorbent cloth and lift solids gently with a spoon. Treat the stain with care so that it does not spread, then press the area dry with an absorbent cloth.

settings.label: Rotation
settings.value: Turn the rug every 3 to 6 months, so that it wears evenly.

settings.label: Sunlight
settings.value: Long exposure to sunlight can fade the colours. Use curtains or blinds to limit direct light on the rug.

settings.label: Furniture
settings.value: Place protectors under the legs of furniture and move it from time to time, to avoid permanent marks.

settings.label: Loose threads
settings.value: If a thread stands above the surface, cut it level with scissors. Do not pull it: more may come loose.

settings.label: Creases
settings.value: Creases left by rolling usually go within a few weeks once the rug lies flat. Rolling it the other way speeds this up.

settings.label: Odour
settings.value: A new rug may have a smell when unpacked. Air the room. If the smell stays, sprinkle baking soda on the rug and vacuum it the next day.

settings.label: Storage
settings.value: Never fold a rug. Roll it tightly around a cardboard tube, keep it off the floor and check it from time to time, to avoid mould and deformation.

settings.label: Professional cleaning
settings.value: For a deeper clean, use a specialised professional. Rugs in Eucalyptus or Viscose: injection-extraction, at low temperature and controlled pressure. Rugs in wool: cleaning with water at no more than 30 °C, with a pH-neutral soap or detergent.

settings.title: Which size for which room
settings.text: Most rooms look better with a rug that is larger than people expect. A rug that is too small leaves the furniture looking as if it is floating.
settings.sizes_label: The five standard sizes drawn one inside the other, to scale
settings.sizes_text: When no standard size fits the room, every rug is made to measure, in any size up to [max_size]. Its page works out the price as you type the size.

settings.drawing_label: Plan of a living room: a sofa and two armchairs with their front legs on a rug, and a strip of floor between the rug and the walls
settings.title: Living room
settings.rule: At least the front legs of all seating on the rug, with 20 to 45 cm of floor visible around the edges.

settings.drawing_label: Plan of a dining room: a table and eight chairs on a rug that extends beyond the table on every side
settings.title: Dining room
settings.rule: The rug extends 60 to 75 cm beyond the table on every side, so that the chairs stay on it when pulled out.
settings.example: A table of 200 × 100 cm needs a rug of at least 320 × 220 cm.

settings.drawing_label: Plan of a bedroom: a rug under the lower part of a bed, extending beyond both sides and beyond the foot
settings.title: Bedroom
settings.rule: The rug extends 50 to 90 cm beyond each side of the bed and past its foot.
settings.example: A bed 180 cm wide needs a rug at least 280 cm wide.

settings.drawing_label: Plan of an open space: one rug under the seating and a second rug under the dining table
settings.title: Open-plan space
settings.rule: One rug per zone, such as seating, dining or reading, each sized to its group of furniture.
